overview: Anthropic’s AI accelerates its own development, raising safety concerns
OpenAI eyes an IPO by 2027 as enterprise revenue surges
Nvidia’s AI chip sales to dubious Chinese firm highlight oversight gaps

top.title: Why a new report on Anthropic automating AI development is alarming researchers
top.summary: METR’s 11‑week probe finds Anthropic’s models improving twice as fast as a year ago, driven by AI‑assisted productivity rather than compute scaling, sparking worries about self‑accelerating AI and transparency.

top.title: Goodbye Claude, Hello Pi
top.summary: A long‑time Claude Code user abandons it for Pi, citing workflow limitations and recent feature changes, reflecting growing developer frustration with Anthropic’s tooling.

top.title: Show HN: We compressed a 31B video+audio diffusion model to 14B, 6 steps, INT8
top.summary: HyperFlow H3 Flash compresses a 31B video‑audio diffusion model to 14B, enabling 6‑step generation on modest hardware using INT8 quantization.

top.title: OpenAI president Greg Brockman says company could be IPO ready in 2027
top.summary: OpenAI president Greg Brockman says the company could be IPO‑ready by 2027, citing strong enterprise growth and recent large‑client wins like JPMorgan.

top.title: The Wizard of Open Weights: Chris Alexiuk Makes AI Easy With Open Models
top.summary: NVIDIA engineer Chris Alexiuk promotes open‑source LLMs, especially Nemotron, arguing openness is essential for democratizing AI and enabling diverse applications.

top.title: The US let Nvidia sell chips to an empty office in China
top.summary: U.S. regulators approve Nvidia H200 chip sales to New Matrix, a seemingly nonexistent Chinese firm linked to a blacklisted private equity group, exposing lax export oversight.
